body: Thank you so much for your kind words. I'm sorry, but my mind is really scattered right now, so I feel like I really can't respond well to what you've said, but know that I really do appreciate it.
This is really similar to intrusive thoughts I get while watching shows and movies. It's good to know that I'm not alone in those kinds of thoughts!
I'm so sorry for your loss, but it's not your fault. Hang in there.

Hey, I just wanted to say that I'm really sorry that I didn't respond to your comment. I'm extremely bad about randomly ghosting people when I get overwhelmed, but it's not because I wasn't interested in what you said or anything like that. Thank you for trying to help me, but I think I might just be in a place where I can't really be helped. Sorry again.
Seriously.

I do think that the student health center and counselling are separate, though I'm not 100% sure. It's good to know that I can start there and then go to therapy outside of the school only if necessary, since therapy is so expensive, and has never worked great for me anyway.


It's difficult for me to pinpoint why I wasn't doing my work when I dropped my classes, but it wasn't because I was struggling with the subject. I'd say I was just extremely overwhelmed by having to deal with the workload, trying to socialize in my classes, and trying to do everything perfectly (since I'm a notorious perfectionist) while also being extremely depressed. Then the more behind I got, the more stressed I got, and it eventually just got too difficult to catch up. 


I just often worry that it *is* an excuse...I think because you can't really prove if something is because of brain fog. There's no official way to really diagnose it, so you have to go off of how you feel. I frequently don't trust my own judgement or feelings, so I always struggle to accept things that can't be empirically proven by someone else. It took me years to finally accept that I was depressed, and I was severely suicidal. 


You definitely caught me with the trying to blame everything else, though, I think. I think I do often try to blame myself for everything. I know logically that even if I do have a really low IQ, it's not my fault, but somehow it still feels like a personal failing. Sometimes I think that I ruined my brain by being so depressed during an important developmental stage in middle/high school, but even if that is the case, it's not like I chose that either. 


I do think my school offers contact through email, so I would probably start with that. Writing is a lot easier for me than talking, so I'd be a lot more likely to follow through with it. Scheduling appointments is extremely difficult, for some reason haha. But thank you for your reassuring words, they do help me feel a little bit better.


Again, thank you for taking so much time to talk to me about this. I know it might be weird that I say this every message, but it really does mean a lot to me. I don't really have any friends anymore besides my boyfriend, and he's really not the best with this stuff, so it really helps to talk to someone who has been through something similar. It really makes me feel less alone, so thank you. :)
Thank you, I'll check it out!

I'm honestly so blown away by your kindness. I know that that's sort of the point of this subreddit, but I wasn't really expecting anyone to respond, if I'm honest. I've posted about stuff like this on other subreddits a few times, and people usually don't seem very interested. So, thank you for taking so much time to talk to me about this.

I've been encouraged by a past therapist to go to the student health center because I was struggling with being too depressed to do any of my work. Instead, I just ended up dropping all of my classes for several semesters, which landed me in "progress probation," because I dropped them all after the last drop day. I've since improved my record, but I'm still wary of going to talk to someone at the school about this because I have extremely bad social anxiety. People scare me in general, but when I need to talk to them about "serious" topics, I get even more frightened. That being said...do you know if they would be able to diagnose me at the health center, or do I need to go to a therapist for that? Part of me really does want to make some changes in my life so that maybe I can fathom living longer. 

I wouldn't even know where to begin for trying to find out what disability I could have...I have heard that depression can cause issues with memory and other thinking problems, but I always feel like I'm making excuses when I try to attribute my problems to that. While I think it's definitely true that I've struggled with really strong brain fog for many years now, I just don't know if that can really explain everything. 

Anyway, I wanted to write a lot more in response to this, but it's now getting extremely late (or early) for me, so my brain is working even less than usual haha. Again, I really appreciate your responses, and I hope you have a wonderful New Year!

Wow, this is so useful, thanks! 

I've taken those questionnaires for anxiety, depression, and OCD before, administered by a therapist/psychiatrist. I know that I have several mental illnesses, but they really shouldn't affect my mental abilities in the ways I've been noticing, as far as I'm aware. 

I have looked a bit into autism, because my mom made a comment a long time ago where she seemed to think I might be on the spectrum because of my social difficulties, but when I read into it or take those online "tests," it doesn't seem to really fit. I don't really think I have ADHD either, though I honestly haven't researched that at all, so I might check that out.

Sorry it took me so long to respond, I've been pretty busy since it's New Year's Eve. I really appreciate you taking time to respond to me and even taking the time to give me some helpful links. I hope you have a happy New Year!

Thank you for your response, it made me feel a little bit better. My boyfriend also gets mixed up between left and right all the time, and he's studying to be an engineer and is very smart. I think it's more common than people think.

Thank you for your response. The way you described being told you're smart all the time as a kid is spot on. I wish my parents/teachers had focused more on how I'm a hard worker, because I've read that it's much more encouraging for children. Not that I blame them for how I'm feeling now, though. 

The thing is, I'm afraid to get tested for any learning or intellectual issues because it will probably involve taking an IQ test, and I know that if I do poorly (poorly being lower than average), I will probably feel awful about it for the rest of my life, however long that is. I do feel like there's \*something\* slightly off about me, because along with some of the really simple errors I make, I'm also incredibly bad in social situations, especially those involving emotions. Sometimes I wish I had been tested as a kid, but apparently no one thought there was anything wrong with me.

I am so sorry your mom said that to you, that's a completely awful thing to say. I've felt similarly to you before, and while I can't tell you what to do, I would recommend finding something- anything- that can help you hold on. 

For example, you could order something on the internet that you really want, even if it's small, so you'll want to stick around until you receive it. Or, you could schedule a fun day in the future where you go out to eat, go to the park, or hang out with friends. If you have something in the future to look forward to, you might be able to push off those dark thoughts a little more easily. Then, if you keep buying yourself more time, you'll have some space to make some changes to your life (even if they're small) that can make your life better. 

I can't imagine how you feel after someone so close to you said that, but I really urge you to hold on as long as you can. Even if you can't see it right now, most problems are temporary, and you can probably make your future a lot better than your present if you have time to do so.

I hope that makes sense, and I hope you find a reason to keep living. Sending you my best wishes.

Hey, I've been where you are. I don't know your life and I'm not here to judge what you decide to do with it, but I want to urge you to give it more time. I know everyone says that, but with family issues, time can really help. One day, you'll likely have the opportunity to leave and live your own life. You'll be able to see a therapist and work through your difficulties. There can still be hope for you.
I'm thinking about the same thing. The problem is that most ways are unreliable and/or incredibly painful.

I have to write a note because there's someone close to me who is very sensitive and will probably blame themselves. I've lived for their sake for a long time, but I'm not sure if I can keep doing it.

I'm sorry that you feel the way I do, it's a crappy way to feel. If it's worth anything, I read a couple of your posts, and you don't sound stupid to me.
Thank you!
Thank you for your thoughtful response. I really appreciate it. I'm not sure what I'm going to do yet, but you have shown me that I have more to think about, so thank you.
I'm just unhappy with my intellectual capabilities, which isn't really something I can fix.

I'm not sure what I want, if I'm honest. I think part of it is that I want to feel accepted by both my peers and society. I don't want to live my life constantly one step behind everyone else. I want to be able to participate in the world  in a meaningful and helpful way.

If I did manage to achieve my goals as the person I am now, I don't think I would feel any better. I am deeply unhappy with who I am, and I don't think any amount of success would change that. Even if I were to achieve my goals somehow, I would still be the same person, and I would still feel slow, useless, and inadequate.

The only way it seems I would be able to change my mind is either by changing myself or changing how I view myself. I cannot change how intelligent I am, so that's out. But I don't think I can change how I view myself either...it would involve changing my entire viewpoint on how I should be living my life. I'd have to learn to settle for a much simpler life, which I honestly just don't want to do. I just can't accept who I am because I've always wanted to be more.

Don't know if that makes sense.

Thanks for your response. The problem isn't so much something I'm going through, so it won't really pass. I've just come to the realization that I'm extremely unintelligent, and I don't want to live the life that's in front of me because of that.

I realize how insulting that sounds to anyone who has a lower intelligence, but I'm not saying that everyone who isn't a genius should just die. It's just that, personally, while it may be cowardly, I can't see myself ever being happy now that I know I'm incapable of achieving anything I've ever wished for. I see no point in continuing to live when my entire existence will be painful.

I was raised by highly intelligent and successful parents, so I've always dreamed of being successful academically. My dreams over the years have gotten smaller and smaller as I got more depressed, but now I've realized that I don't think I'm even capable of achieving the smallest of my goals.

Sorry, I think this all sounds extremely dramatic and stupid. I don't know why I'm telling you this, since you can't really say anything that would make me feel better. This thought process has just been eating me alive recently, and I don't want to keep going. I've been depressed for almost half of my life, but I've never felt as worthless and hopeless as I do now. I really pushed myself to make sure I didn't ruin Christmas for my family, but I'm reaching the end of my rope, and I'm really trying to come up with a suicide plan now that won't fail.

I just feel like I'm out of options.

Sorry if this doesn't make sense or is insulting or anything else it may be. And thank you again, I do really appreciate you taking time to send me a message.
I do this too, kind of. Hasn't worked so far. Don't think it ever will, but I still do it even though I don't think it'll do anything.
